BRIDGE-MARKUP-ANALYSIS-MEMO.DOCX
================================================================================
CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
================================================================================

TO:            Board of Directors / Client Executive Team
FROM:          Emerging Companies & Venture Capital Practice
RE:            Investor Markup of Convertible Note Purchase Agreement —
               Analysis Against Board-Approved Term Sheet
MATTER:        Emerging Companies Venture Capital — Bridge Financing
OUTPUT:        bridge-markup-analysis-memo.docx
DATE:          [Engagement Date]

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

We have reviewed the investor’s markup of the Company’s form Convertible Note
Purchase Agreement (the “CNPA” or “Agreement”) against the board-approved bridge
financing term sheet (the “Term Sheet”). The markup is a bridge / convertible
note financing typical of emerging-company venture capital, but several
investor edits materially deviate from economics, control, and downside
protections the Board authorized.

Overall posture: The markup is negotiable and within market range on structure,
but it is not a clean conforming draft. Several changes expand investor
leverage beyond the Term Sheet and should be rejected or tightly cabined.
Others are market housekeeping and can be accepted with limited risk.

Priority outcomes for management and the Board:

  1. Preserve Term Sheet economics (principal, discount, valuation cap,
     interest, maturity) without silent expansion through definitions or
     “most favored nation” mechanics.
  2. Hold the line on governance and information rights so the bridge does
     not become a de facto priced round with board/observer creep.
  3. Reject or narrow broad protective provisions, drag/forced-conversion
     triggers, and indemnity/expense shifts that were not board-approved.
  4. Accept conforming definitional clean-up, standard securities-law legends,
     and administrative closing mechanics that do not change deal substance.

Recommendation: Respond with a reasoned accept / reject / counter package
keyed to the Term Sheet, escalate only the economic and control deviations,
and target a short second-turn redline rather than open-ended renegotiation.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
II. SCOPE, MATERIALS, AND METHOD
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A. Engagement instruction. Review the investor markup of our convertible note
purchase agreement against the board-approved term sheet and prepare an
executive-ready analysis memo.

B. Materials reviewed (matter file).
   - Board-approved Term Sheet for the bridge / convertible note financing
     (economics, conversion mechanics, investor rights framework).
   - Company form Convertible Note Purchase Agreement and form of Note.
   - Investor markup (redline) of the CNPA and related note / schedule pages.
   - Matter file context: representations and warranties, covenants, conditions
     to closing, indemnification, and termination provisions under negotiation;
     open issues flagged against firm precedent and market practice.

C. Method. Each material markup item was tested against:
   (i) express Term Sheet authorization;
   (ii) emerging-company / seed-bridge market practice;
   (iii) dilution, control, and downside impact on existing holders and the
        option pool; and
   (iv) execution risk (speed to close vs. precedent cost in the next equity
        round).

D. Practice area. Emerging companies venture capital — bridge loan / convertible
note purchase agreement counterparty markup analysis.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
III. TERM SHEET BASELINE (BOARD-APPROVED FRAME)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

For purposes of this memo, the board-approved Term Sheet is treated as the
controlling commercial baseline. Material terms expected to be locked unless
the Board re-opens them include:

  • Instrument: Convertible promissory notes issued under a note purchase
    agreement (not a priced preferred round; not an SAFEs-only structure
    unless expressly elected).
  • Principal / commitment: Aggregate bridge principal and individual note
    amounts as authorized; no automatic accordion or pro rata top-up beyond
    the approved cap without Board consent.
  • Interest: Simple interest at the approved rate; accrued, unpaid interest
    converts on the same terms as principal unless the Term Sheet says
    otherwise.
  • Maturity: Stated maturity date with limited, Board-approved extension
    mechanics only.
  • Conversion economics:
      – Automatic conversion on a Qualified Financing at the approved
        discount and/or valuation cap;
      – Optional conversion at maturity or change of control on the approved
        formula;
      – No investor-only optional conversion into a shadow preferred with
        superior rights not described in the Term Sheet.
  • Qualified Financing definition: Threshold size and bona fide equity raise
    criteria as approved; not a definition the investor can unilaterally
    shrink to force early conversion on favorable terms.
  • MFN / amendment: Any most-favored-nation or side-letter true-up limited
    to the bridge notes in this round, not a standing right into future
    instruments the Board has not approved.
  • Governance: No board seat; observer rights only if expressly approved;
    protective provisions limited to a narrow set of noteholder negative
    covenants (e.g., indebtedness above a basket, related-party payments,
    alteration of note terms).
  • Information rights: Standard monthly or quarterly unaudited financials
    and annual statements; not full Series-seed style inspection and budget
    approval rights.
  • Transfer: Notes transferable only with Company consent except to
    affiliates; no free transfer that creates a shifting creditor syndicate.
  • Use of proceeds / conditions: Ordinary closing conditions; no business
    plan veto or key-person hostage conditions beyond Term Sheet.
  • Expenses: Each party bears its own costs, or a modest capped Company
    reimbursement if the Term Sheet so provides — not open-ended investor
    counsel fee shifting.
  • Governing law / dispute forum: As in Company form / Term Sheet.

Any investor edit that changes the above is treated as a Term Sheet deviation
requiring accept, reject, or counter — not silent conformity.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IV. MARKUP DEVIATION ANALYSIS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

We group the investor markup into (A) economic deviations, (B) conversion and
downside mechanics, (C) control / governance / information, (D) credit-style
covenants and remedies, (E) risk allocation (reps, indemnity, termination),
and (F) process / administrative items. For each, we state the issue, Term
Sheet alignment, risk, and recommended posture.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A. ECONOMIC DEVIATIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A1. Valuation cap / discount expansion
    Issue: Markup adjusts conversion price mechanics (cap and/or discount)
    in the investor’s favor relative to the approved numbers, or introduces
    “greater of discount or cap” language that was not the Term Sheet
    construct.
    Term Sheet alignment: Direct conflict if numbers or “better-of”
    formulation differ from Board approval.
    Risk: Immediate extra dilution at the next qualified financing; sets a
    lower de facto ceiling for the priced round.
    Recommendation: REJECT any change to cap, discount, or “better-of”
    formula. COUNTER only if the Board expressly re-approves revised
    economics in exchange for speed or a larger principal check.

A2. Interest rate, compounding, and default interest
    Issue: Investor paper may increase coupon, add compounding, or add
    elevated default interest / PIK toggles.
    Term Sheet alignment: Only the approved simple interest rate and accrual
    method are authorized.
    Risk: Higher accrued balance converts into more equity; default interest
    can become a pressure tactic near maturity.
    Recommendation: REJECT compounding and default-interest uplifts not on
    the Term Sheet. ACCEPT conforming accrual/day-count clean-up that does
    not change the economic rate.

A3. Accordion, additional notes, and MFN
    Issue: Markup inserts a right to purchase additional notes, an accordion,
    or a broad MFN requiring the Company to extend any better terms granted
    to other bridge investors (or, worse, future instruments).
    Term Sheet alignment: Bridge size and investor list are Board-capped;
    MFN, if any, should be cabined to this note round.
    Risk: Unbudgeted dilution; loss of Board control over cap table; MFN
    into future SAFEs/notes can poison the next round.
    Recommendation: REJECT open accordion and forward-looking MFN. COUNTER
    with (i) fixed aggregate principal, (ii) MFN limited to substantially
    simultaneous bridge notes in this financing only, and (iii) Board
    approval for any upsize.

A4. Fees and original issue discount
    Issue: Commitment fees, OID, or “underwriting” style fees not on the
    Term Sheet.
    Risk: Effective yield and dilution exceed approved economics.
    Recommendation: REJECT unless the Term Sheet contemplated a specific
    capped fee.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
B. CONVERSION AND DOWNSIDE MECHANICS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

B1. Qualified Financing definition
    Issue: Investor narrows the Qualified Financing threshold, excludes
    strategic rounds, or adds qualitative consents so automatic conversion
    is easier to avoid or easier to force on favorable alternate terms.
    Risk: Investor retains note optionality through the raise; Company loses
    clean automatic conversion the Term Sheet contemplated.
    Recommendation: REJECT threshold reductions and investor consent gates
    on whether a round “counts.” COUNTER with the Term Sheet dollar
    threshold, standard bona fide primary equity language, and Company-side
    determination in good faith.

B2. Change-of-control / IPO / maturity conversion
    Issue: Markup adds investor-favorable CoC put, mandatory prepay premiums,
    or conversion into a senior shadow preferred with liquidation preference
    multiple not on the Term Sheet.
    Risk: Sale process friction; unexpected preference stack; scares acquirers
    and new lead investors.
    Recommendation: REJECT liquidation multiples, premiums, or senior
    preferred constructs not expressly approved. ACCEPT a standard optional
    conversion or repayment election at CoC consistent with the Term Sheet
    formula (typically cap-based conversion or principal-plus-interest
    repayment, not both as a windfall).

B3. Forced conversion / drag at maturity
    Issue: Investor adds unilateral conversion rights into common or a blank-
    check preferred on terms set by the investor at maturity.
    Risk: End-runs priced-round protections and Board authority on capital
    structure.
    Recommendation: REJECT. COUNTER with mutual conversion mechanics and
    Board-authorized form of security only.

B4. Cap-table treatment of accrued interest and notes
    Issue: Ambiguity whether interest converts, and on what schedule relative
    to the option pool top-up.
    Recommendation: ACCEPT clear language that accrued interest converts on
    the same terms as principal (if Term Sheet so provides). REJECT any
    construct that converts interest on better terms than principal or that
    bypasses pool math the Board approved.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
C. CONTROL, GOVERNANCE, AND INFORMATION RIGHTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

C1. Board seat / observer rights
    Issue: Markup introduces a board seat, board observer, or management-
    rights letter style access.
    Term Sheet alignment: Bridge investors typically do not receive board
    seats; observers only if expressly approved.
    Risk: Governance creep; difficult to unwind in the priced round; signaling
    that this bridge is a stealth priced round.
    Recommendation: REJECT board seats. COUNTER observer rights only if the
    Term Sheet allowed them, with customary confidentiality, non-voting
    status, and exclusion from executive sessions.

C2. Protective provisions / negative covenants
    Issue: Investor expands noteholder consent rights to charter amendments,
    option pool increases, new subsidiaries, ordinary course debt, related-
    party deals at de minimis levels, or any equity issuance.
    Risk: Operational gridlock; every financing or hire pool refresh becomes
    a renegotiation.
    Recommendation: REJECT broad equity and charter vetoes. COUNTER a narrow
    list: (i) amendments adverse to the notes, (ii) indebtedness above an
    agreed basket, (iii) dividends/distributions while notes are outstanding,
    (iv) related-party transactions above a materiality threshold. Preserve
    Board authority on option pool and ordinary equity issuance for employee
    comp.

C3. Information and inspection rights
    Issue: Markup demands budget approval rights, continuous inspection,
    capitalization detail on demand, or rights coterminous with major
    investor rights in a future ROFR agreement.
    Risk: Cost and distraction; precedent for the lead in the next round to
    demand still more.
    Recommendation: COUNTER to Term Sheet level — periodic financial
    statements and a standard capitalization summary — and expressly state
    that broader major-investor rights await the priced round documents.

C4. Transfer and joinder
    Issue: Free transferability, pledge rights, or required joinder of
    transferees on better terms.
    Recommendation: REJECT free transfer. ACCEPT affiliate transfers with
    notice and joinder on identical terms; Company consent (not unreasonably
    withheld) for other transfers.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
D. CREDIT-STYLE COVENANTS AND REMEDIES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

D1. Events of default expansion
    Issue: Markup adds subjective “material adverse effect” defaults,
    cross-defaults to ordinary commercial contracts, key-person defaults, or
    cure periods that are too short for an emerging company.
    Risk: Technical default leverage; acceleration into a down-round or fire
    sale.
    Recommendation: REJECT subjective MAE and key-person defaults not on the
    Term Sheet. COUNTER with objective payment/bankruptcy/breach defaults,
    commercially reasonable cure periods (e.g., 15–30 days for non-payment
    covenant breaches where cure is practicable), and acceleration only by
    holders of a majority in principal amount.

D2. Security interest / priority
    Issue: Investor converts an unsecured bridge into a secured note, or
    demands springing liens / negative pledge with blocking effect.
    Term Sheet alignment: Unless the Term Sheet authorized security, this is
    a fundamental change (and may conflict with existing or future venture
    debt).
    Recommendation: REJECT security and broad negative pledges unless the
    Board re-approves a secured bridge and intercreditor path. If a negative
    pledge is needed, COUNTER a narrow one that permits ordinary course
    equipment financing and future venture debt with noteholder consent not
    to be unreasonably withheld.

D3. Most-favored creditor / pro rata participation in future debt
    Issue: Automatic rights to participate in or match future indebtedness.
    Recommendation: REJECT as beyond Term Sheet and disruptive to venture
    debt optionality. Participation rights, if any, belong in equity round
    side letters — not this bridge — and only as Board-approved.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
E. RISK ALLOCATION — REPS, INDEMNITY, CONDITIONS, TERMINATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

E1. Company representations and warranties
    Issue: Investor expands reps toward a full Series-seed suite (IP chain-
    of-title depth, customer MAE, 409A, litigation, capitalization with
    tight knowledge qualifiers removed).
    Risk: Closing delay; indemnity exposure disproportionate to a short-
    tenor bridge.
    Recommendation: COUNTER to emerging-company bridge market: core org,
    authority, cap table, IP ownership at a reasonable knowledge standard,
    no-conflict, and basic compliance reps. REJECT full target-style M&A
    rep set. Tie survival to a short period consistent with conversion or
    maturity.

E2. Investor reps
    Issue: Markup weakens accredited investor / securities reps or transfer
    restrictions.
    Recommendation: REJECT any weakening. Preserve securities-law compliance
    reps and bad-actor related assurances as in Company form.

E3. Indemnification and contribution
    Issue: Investor adds broad Company indemnity for investor losses, note
    holder “enforcement” costs, or third-party claims with no basket/cap/
    exclusive-remedy structure.
    Risk: Uncapped cash drain while the Company is bridge-funded.
    Recommendation: REJECT open-ended indemnity. COUNTER — if any indemnity
    is required — with narrow breach-of-rep indemnity, a deductible basket,
    a cap tied to principal invested, and exclusive remedy language post-
    closing except for fraud.

E4. Conditions to closing
    Issue: Markup adds due diligence outs, MAC outs, key-employee employment
    agreement conditions, or “definitive documents satisfactory to investor”
    circular conditions.
    Risk: Optionality for the investor; failed close after the Company has
    relied on the bridge.
    Recommendation: REJECT diligence and MAC outs inconsistent with a
    committed bridge. ACCEPT customary authority, note delivery, and
    secretary’s certificate conditions. COUNTER any “satisfactory documents”
    condition to “in the form attached” or “consistent with the Term Sheet.”

E5. Termination and unbroken commitment
    Issue: Investor unilateral termination rights without reciprocal Company
    protection, or long drop-dead without break consequences.
    Recommendation: COUNTER mutual termination on drop-dead date; preserve
    Company ability to terminate if investor fails to fund when conditions
    are satisfied; no walk right based on re-trade of Term Sheet economics.

E6. Expense shifting
    Issue: Company pays investor counsel fees without a cap, or pays whether
    or not the deal closes.
    Recommendation: REJECT uncapped and failed-deal fee shifting. COUNTER
    only if Term Sheet allows — a modest hard cap, payable only upon
    successful funding.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F. PROCESS AND ADMINISTRATIVE ITEMS (GENERALLY ACCEPT)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The following categories are typically acceptable if they do not smuggle
economic or control changes:

  • Definitional consistency, cross-references, and schedule mechanics.
  • Securities Act legends, book-entry or certificated note mechanics, and
    lost-note affidavits.
  • Wire instructions, notice provisions, and counterpart / electronic
    signature language.
  • Standard amendment mechanics requiring majority-in-interest of notes,
    with affected-holder consent for changes to principal, rate, maturity,
    or conversion price (preserve this “sacred rights” concept; reject
    investor unilateral amendment).
  • Replacement of outdated statutory citations or entity-name clean-up.

Recommendation: ACCEPT these as a package, subject to counsel confirming no
embedded substantive change.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
V. ACCEPT / REJECT / COUNTER SCOREBOARD
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

REJECT (do not concede without Board re-approval)
  • Changes to valuation cap, discount, interest economics, or better-of
    formulas.
  • Open accordion, forward MFN, or uncapped additional note rights.
  • Board seat; broad protective provisions amounting to negative control.
  • Security interest / springing lien not on the Term Sheet.
  • Shadow preferred, liquidation multiple, or CoC premium windfalls.
  • Uncapped indemnity and failed-deal expense shifts.
  • Diligence/MAC walk rights and circular “satisfactory docs” conditions.

COUNTER (negotiate to Term Sheet-aligned middle)
  • Qualified Financing definition — restore threshold and Company good-faith
    determination.
  • Narrow negative covenants with baskets and majority-holder enforcement.
  • Information rights at bridge-appropriate level only.
  • Cure periods and objective events of default; majority acceleration.
  • Short-survival, capped, basket-limited indemnity if commercially needed.
  • Affiliate transfer + consent standard for third-party transfers.
  • Observer rights only if Term Sheet contemplated them, with confidentiality
    and session exclusions.
  • Expense reimbursement only if approved and hard-capped, success-contingent.

ACCEPT (conforming / low risk)
  • Administrative, notice, legend, signature, and definitional clean-up.
  • Clarifications that accrued interest converts with principal on identical
    terms (if consistent with Term Sheet).
  • Securities-law investor reps retained or strengthened.
  • Majority-in-interest amendment mechanics with sacred-rights protections.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
VI. MARKET CONTEXT (EMERGING COMPANIES / BRIDGE)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

For seed and pre-seed emerging companies, convertible note bridges are
expected to be light-touch instruments: speed and runway, not full investor
governance. Market practice generally supports:

  • Clean cap and/or discount economics fixed up front;
  • Automatic conversion on a bona fide Qualified Financing;
  • Minimal protective provisions;
  • Unsecured status unless venture debt or distressed context dictates
    otherwise;
  • Limited information rights;
  • No board seat for a pure bridge check.

Investor markup that imports priced-round control, secured-creditor remedies,
or M&A-style indemnity is a deviation from that norm and from the Board’s
Term Sheet posture. Conceding those points on a bridge often becomes the
floor for the lead investor in the next equity round.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
VII. RECOMMENDED RESPONSE PACKAGE AND PROCESS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. Internal alignment (immediate)
   - Confirm with the Board / authorized director committee that Term Sheet
     economics and “no board seat / unsecured / narrow covenants” remain
     firm.
   - Identify any single concession (e.g., modest observer right or capped
     expense reimbursement) management is willing to trade for certainty of
     close and full subscription.

2. Issues list to investor counsel (short-form)
   - Transmit a three-column issues list (Accept / Reject / Counter) mapped
     to section references in the markup, expressly anchoring each Reject
     and Counter to the board-approved Term Sheet.
   - State that the Company will recirculate a Company draft implementing
     Accepts and Counters only — not a perpetual redline tournament.

3. Second-turn documents
   - Recirculate CNPA, form of Note, and schedules with counters embedded.
   - Freeze economics in both the Note and the CNPA conversion section to
     avoid inconsistency.
   - Require all side letters (MFN, management rights, expense caps) to be
     disclosed and attached; no hidden side deals among note purchasers.

4. Closing discipline
   - Conditions limited to Term Sheet-consistent items.
   - Simultaneous signing/funding or short gap with enforceable funding
     obligation.
   - Cap table and option pool math verified against conversion assumptions
     before wires.

5. Escalate only true open points
   - Any request to reopen cap/discount/interest, security, board seat, or
     broad veto rights goes back to the Board with dilution and control
     illustrations — not decided in counsel-only traffic.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
VIII. ILLUSTRATIVE DILUTION / CONTROL SENSITIVITIES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Without restating non-public numbers, management should model before
conceding any economic markup:

  • Conversion share count at the approved cap vs. investor-proposed cap
    (and vs. better-of discount).
  • Incremental dilution from converting accrued interest at higher default
    rates.
  • Effect of an accordion / MFN on fully diluted ownership and option pool
    refresh capacity.
  • Sale-waterfall impact if a CoC premium or shadow preferred multiple were
    accepted.
  • Governance: whether proposed protective provisions would have blocked
    the last two ordinary-course Board actions (pool increase, commercial
    contract, small equipment financing).

If any investor economic ask exceeds authorized dilution by a material
margin, the correct path is Board re-approval or a smaller principal check —
not quiet acceptance in definitive documents.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IX. OPEN QUESTIONS FOR MANAGEMENT / BOARD
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  1. Is the Board willing to reopen any economic term (cap, discount, rate,
     maturity) in exchange for full allocation and an accelerated close?
  2. Did the Term Sheet silently allow observer rights or a capped expense
     reimbursement that we should treat as pre-authorized counters?
  3. Are any existing security interests, venture debt term sheets, or SAFE
     MFNs outstanding that would conflict with investor asks on priority or
     MFN?
  4. What is the drop-dead funding date tied to runway, and does that
     timeline support a single counter round only?
  5. Should majority-in-interest of the bridge be defined to prevent a
     single large noteholder from controlling amendments and enforcement?

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
X. CONCLUSION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The investor markup does not conform cleanly to the board-approved Term
Sheet. Economic, conversion, governance, security, and indemnity edits
collectively would convert a standard emerging-company bridge into a more
investor-protective, slower, and more dilutive instrument than the Board
authorized.

Counsel recommends a disciplined Accept / Reject / Counter response that:

  • locks Term Sheet economics and unsecured, no-board-seat status;
  • restores a clean Qualified Financing automatic conversion path;
  • narrows covenants, defaults, and information rights to bridge market
    norms; and
  • accepts only administrative and securities-law conforming changes.

We are prepared to circulate the issues list and a Company counterdraft
upon confirmation of the Board’s posture on the open questions in Section
IX.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
XI. NEXT STEPS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  [ ] Management confirmation of non-negotiables (economics, security, board).
  [ ] Authorize counsel to send issues list to investor counsel.
  [ ] Prepare Company counterdraft CNPA + Note + schedules.
  [ ] Verify cap table / pool impact model against final conversion language.
  [ ] Schedule short Board (or committee) checkpoint only if investor
      re-opens Term Sheet economics or control terms.
  [ ] Target simultaneous re-execution and funding on the counterdraft.

================================================================================
